fallos_mitigaciones: 'Wrong-time retrieval' (S2.3.1): unordered embedding-similarity records do not encode temporal order/predecessor relations, so a query like 'Where did Bob live before moving to Miami?' can retrieve the wrong time point (answering 'Boston' or 'Miami' instead of the correct intermediate 'Davis'); mitigated via MemTree's explicit leaf-order temporal hierarchy. Separately, mutable-profile designs face a 'growing-or-compressing dilemma' (S2.3.2): keeping all evidence makes maintenance cost grow with N, while compression discards intermediate states/transition evidence; mitigated via the persistent/derived-artifact separation with localized per-node dirty-path refresh.
cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemForest: An Efficient Agent Memory System with Hierarchical Temporal Indexing.
notes: S3.1: canonical facts (temporally-anchored, retrieval-ready text + source refs + entity mentions) are the stable write unit -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA(temporal state trajectories/event evidence, e.g. the Bob-residence example)+SEMANTICA(entity/user facts). representacion=HIBRIDA: MemTree is a hierarchical TIME-ORDERED TREE index (S3.2, Fig.4: leaves=time-local evidence, internal nodes=interval summaries, root=coarse recall) PLUS derived node embeddings for retrieval -> both tree/graph-structural and vector. operaciones=WRITE(parallel chunk extraction into canonical facts, S3.1)+CONSOLIDACION('Canonical fact consolidation repairs the semantic fragmentation inherently introduced by' parallel extraction, S3 intro)+ACTUALIZACION(S3.1 'a later update only needs to invalidate and regenerate the derived artifacts whose dependency paths intersect the affected scopes' -- localized per-node dirty-path refresh, Table1 O(log N) critical path). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (each new session/chunk arrival deterministically triggers extraction+local MemTree insertion). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(node embeddings, derived-artifact layer)+RANKING(coarse-to-fine interval-summary browsing, S3.2)+GRAFO(hierarchical tree traversal root->leaf, Fig.3 Tree Browser). mide_lectura=SI: pass@1/pass@8 accuracy on LongMemEval-S/LoCoMo is the paper's central metric (Table/Fig.1b efficiency-accuracy frontier) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION(session trees preserve per-session chronology)+PROYECTO(entity/scene trees persist across MANY sessions, a user's whole multi-year history, S3.2). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the paper's central concern IS temporal-state consistency/correctness across evolving memory (avoiding 'wrong-time retrieval', preserving historical/transition states rather than a single mutable latest-state summary that silently loses intermediate truth) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Fig.1: MemForest achieves 79.8% pass@1 on LongMemEval-S (best among stateful baselines) while sustaining ~6x higher write throughput than EverMemOS -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;LATENCIA;COSTO-TOKENS ('avoid unnecessary LLM calls and token usage', S2.4). Section6 dedicated ablation studies of design choices (parallel extraction, MemTree vs flat/mutable alternatives) -> ABLATION. F_screening was RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD.

benchmarks: ScaleWoB (96 web apps, 86 train / 10 held-out test)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Agent memory lacks reliable step-level supervision: we usually do not know what each memory state should encode... Latent memory is usually more efficient but much harder to supervise, because its compressed vectors lack human-readable semantics' (S1); mitigated via novelty-driven joint training that provides 'natural, annotation-free supervision for the memory module' using deterministic code-coverage signals. Separately, a comparative failure mode: 'local baselines exhibit an early plateau due to premature exploration stagnation... these methods prune their context, inevitably discarding critical historical information as the session progresses' (S4.2), contrasted with JAMEL's non-pruning latent compression that avoids context truncation entirely.
cita: Tian et al. (2026). Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals.
notes: S3.2/Eq.4-5: each historical (observation,action) pair is compressed by a FROZEN vision-language model into a single latent EOS-token embedding hi; Mt=[h1,...,ht-1] is the full memory state, projected via a learned linear aligner W into the POLICY's embedding space and prepended as a soft prefix -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(bounded per-episode/session working state, not a persisted cross-session store)+PARAMETRICA(non-textual, opaque continuous vector representation injected directly into the model's embedding space, explicitly contrasted against 'explicit textual memories' which 'are interpretable... can be inspected, revised, or heuristically filtered', S1). representacion=VECTOR (dense embedding tokens, no text/graph/doc storage). operaciones=WRITE ONLY: each step is compressed and appended to the growing sequence Mt, with NO admission/consolidation/forgetting/update -- all latent tokens are retained ('JAMEL aligns with this comprehensive retention strategy by avoiding context truncation. Instead, JAMEL compresses all historical information into latent memory tokens', S4.2). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(each interaction step deterministically triggers compression+append, Eq.4). retrieval=NA: there is no selective search/ranking mechanism -- the ENTIRE memory sequence is always prepended wholesale as a soft prefix (Eq.5), exactly analogous to a full-inclusion (non-retrieval) memory design. mide_lectura=SI: the ENTIRE experimental design (Table1 baseline comparison, ablation-like per-app breakdown Fig.3, Case Study S4.3) directly tests whether the memory-conditioned policy successfully USES accumulated history to avoid repeating exhausted behaviors and discover novel states -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=TAREA: memory is scoped to ONE bounded app-exploration session/task (T=50 steps per app), not a persisted cross-day store. multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Table1/Fig.2: JAMEL-9B reaches 20.7 avg cumulative reward, competitive with cloud ReAct-vision(20.9) and exceeding ReAct-text(19.9), while clearly beating open-weight MAI-UI-8B(8.4) and Mobile-Agent-v3.5(5.9) -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Table2: JAMEL uses 2.76x/2.81x/17.85x/21.92x FEWER input tokens than Mobile-Agent-v3.5/MAI-UI/ReAct-Text/ReAct-Vision respectively -> COSTO in F, metricas=COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO. S4.3 Case Study: JAMEL's OWN failure mode is explicitly documented -- on Pinduoduo, 'persistent modal overlays' cause 'prolonged plateaus... exceptionally dense interfaces can still challenge the compressed memory representation' -> NEGATIVO(a)-style honest limitation, evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA (per-app qualitative pattern analysis, Fig.3, not a controlled with/without-memory ablation). F_screening was COSTO; full text confirms it and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO.

fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's central diagnostic finding IS the failure mode: 'these design choices drastically and asymmetrically redistribute cost... These costs are invisible to accuracy metrics, yet critically dominate at deployment scale' (S1) -- e.g. Paradigm III/IV systems shift majority of end-to-end ENERGY into construction (invisible at query time, Fig.3), spanning a 26.7x energy range (BM25 582kJ to Letta 15,429kJ, Table3) that accuracy-only benchmarks completely hide. Mitigation is operational, not architectural: 'we derive 10 system recommendations covering construction scheduling, capability floors, amortization via query volume, freshness-latency tradeoffs, and fleet-scale management' (Abstract). Section4.6 further identifies the freshness-latency tradeoff: when construction lags session arrival, a system must either block queries until writes commit or SERVE STALE memory.
cita: Omri et al. (2026). Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads.
notes: This is a pure SYSTEMS-CHARACTERIZATION / profiling paper, not a memory mechanism: 'We present the first systems characterization of agent memory' (Abstract), building 'a system-oriented taxonomy classifying agent memory systems along four axes' and 'a phase-aware profiling harness' to CHARACTERIZE TEN EXISTING systems (long_context, BM25, embedRAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG v2, Mem0, SimpleMem, A-Mem, Letta, MIRIX, Table1) spanning four paradigms, without proposing its own mechanism -> mem_tipos=NA/representacion=NA/operaciones=NA/trigger=NA (rule5: explains what it MEASURES instead, below). retrieval=NA: characterizes the varied retrieval pipelines of the ten evaluated systems (lexical/dense/graph-expand/PPR-rerank/tool-mediated) rather than proposing its own. mide_lectura=SI: the entire profiling harness measures per-phase (construction/retrieval/generation) latency, token volume, GPU energy, and accuracy across systems (Fig.2-3, Table3) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO mandatory in F (rule3). alcance=SESION (LongMemEval_S_*/MemoryArena multi-session; each sample ~360K tokens history, 60 queries). multiagente=NO (MIRIX 'multi-type routing' across episodic/semantic/procedural/resource stores is NOT multi-agent sharing). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Section4.6 explicitly studies the 'freshness-latency tradeoff' -- whether a system serves STALE memory when construction lags behind session arrival -- a direct staleness/consistency concern -> FIDELIDAD in F. Fig.2: on LongMemEval_S_*, Mem0 achieves <0.1s/query vs ~38s for long-context (GPT-4.1-mini) while matching/exceeding accuracy -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Table3: end-to-end energy spans 26.7x (BM25 582kJ -> Letta 15,429kJ); normalized J-per-correct-answer spans from BM25's 4,145J floor to MIRIX's 144,629J (a 28-47x premium) -> MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. NEGATIVO in F: 'These costs are invisible to accuracy metrics' is itself P5-style negative evidence about how memory systems are currently EVALUATED (accuracy-only benchmarks systematically hide massive, deployment-critical cost disparities). F_screening was COSTO; full text confirms it and adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: Synthetic Multi-Turn Corpus (own, 3 scenarios: standard/memory_heavy/retrieval_heavy, 20 turns/50 docs each); Real Research Corpus (own, 10 canonical NLP papers)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Existing frameworks treat context assembly as a concatenation problem: rank by relevance, truncate to fit' (Abstract) -- (1) budget partitioning is hardcoded/absent, (2) retrieval is query-only and ignores what the agent already knows, causing token waste on redundant chunks that overlap working memory, (3) memory management (MemGPT/Letta, Mem0, Zep) 'relies on hand-crafted rules for consolidation, eviction, and decay' that cannot adapt; mitigated via the query-aware budget allocator, memory-conditioned MMR-style retriever (Eq.1), and Ebbinghaus-decay consolidation engine respectively. Honest self-reported tradeoff: COMA's groundedness score is LOWER than Naive RAG (0.464 vs 0.687) because 'the judge scores groundedness relative to retrieved chunks only, penalizing answers that draw on working memory items promoted from prior turns' (S6) -- a measurement artifact, not a real quality deficit.
cita: Biswas (2026). COMA: Adaptive Context Budget Management for Memory-Augmented RAG via Query-Aware Zone Allocation, Memory-Conditioned Retrieval, and Cognitive Memory Consolidation.
notes: S3.D: three-tier Atkinson-Shiffrin-inspired architecture -- Tier1 sensory buffer (per-turn staging, ephemeral)+Tier2 WORKING MEMORY (bounded 50-item store)+Tier3 long-term memory (persistent, FAISS-indexed) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO(explicit 'Working Memory' tier)+EPISODICA(one of the 5 prompt-assembly ZONES is explicitly 'episodic' = prior conversation turns, and long-term store generically holds conversational facts/experiences). representacion=VECTOR (FAISS dense embeddings throughout, no graph/doc-file store). operaciones: WRITE(sensory ingestion)+ADMISION(S3.E 'Extract: items with importance score>=0.3 are promoted' sensory->working -- an explicit write-admission gate)+CONSOLIDACION(named 'Memory Consolidation Engine', S3.E: Consolidate working->long-term + Merge pairwise-cosine-similarity>0.85 dedup of long-term items, 'prevents semantic fragmentation')+OLVIDO(Decay Sweep archives items below Ebbinghaus-retention threshold theta=0.3, Eq.5)+ACTUALIZACION(working-memory eviction priority P(m,t) Eq.4 recomputed with recency/frequency on every access). trigger=PRESUPUESTO(consolidation triggered 'when working memory utilization exceeds 80%', S3.E)+CHECKPOINT(the full consolidation cycle 'runs every N=5 turns', S3.E). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(FAISS ANN cosine similarity, Stage1)+RANKING(Eq.1 memory-conditioned MMR-style reranking penalizing candidates overlapping working memory, Stage2). mide_lectura=SI: the paper introduces a dedicated MemoryRecall@K metric (Eq.7) plus 3 other custom metrics measuring context-memory read quality -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (20-turn multi-turn conversational scenarios). multiagente=NO ('multi-agent memory sharing' explicitly listed as future work, not implemented). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: each working-memory item explicitly carries 'source provenance' + a SHA-256 hash index prevents duplicate insertion into long-term memory (S3.D.3) -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table IV/V: COMA achieves 37.1% lower token usage (99,585 vs 158,233 on the real research corpus), 2x higher MemoryRecall@20 (1.000 vs 0.000 for Naive RAG/No-Memory), and 5.4x ContextEfficiency vs Naive RAG -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA. Explicit 3-baseline ablation (Naive RAG/Fixed Allocation/No Memory) isolates each of COMA's 3 components' individual contribution -> ABLATION. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO.

benchmarks: LoCoMo; scaled LoCoMo-style (3x, 10x longer conversations, own); LongMemEvalS
fallos_mitigaciones: 'As interactions accumulate, the memory store grows without bound and fills with redundant entries that inflate storage cost and degrade retrieval by crowding out the most useful evidence,' especially acute on resource-constrained/on-device platforms with hard memory budgets (S1); mitigated via storage-budgeted LLM-guided compression that defers delete/merge/preserve decisions to factual judgment rather than surface similarity. Critique of single-criterion baselines: 'two textually similar entries may carry redundant facts that can be removed, complementary facts that should be merged, or distinct facts that both warrant preservation' -- fixed-similarity-threshold (RuleSim) and PageRank-centrality (RulePR) heuristics cannot distinguish these three cases and are empirically shown to underperform the LLM judge (Fig.4).
cita: Kim et al. (2026). MemRefine: LLM-Guided Compression for Long-Term Agent Memory.
notes: S3: MemRefine is explicitly a POST-CONSTRUCTION module inserted 'after memory construction and before retrieval, leaving the host construction and retrieval pipelines unchanged' -- it operates over entries with 'textual content, an embedding vector, and, depending on the host framework, links/timestamps/metadata' (S3.1) drawn from example entries about factual/biographical content (Fig.2: 'Jon has danced since childhood...') -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA. representacion=HIBRIDA: validated on BOTH an A-MEM-style GRAPH of linked structured notes AND the non-graph Mem0 vector-entry pipeline, explicitly framework-agnostic (S4 'Memory frameworks'). operaciones: NO WRITE (explicitly decoupled from construction: 'all judge and merge calls are issued during memory maintenance rather than at query time... the host construction and retrieval pipelines remain untouched', S3.2 Practical Implications) and NO ADMISION (operates only on EXISTING items, never admits new ones) -> CONSOLIDACION(explicit MERGE action, Algorithm1 line13-17: an LLM synthesizes one entry from two, inheriting union-of-links, recomputed embedding)+OLVIDO(explicit DELETE action, Algorithm1 line10-12, pruning dangling links). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: the entire compression loop is explicitly gated by a fixed storage-budget ratio rho, 'while size(M')>B' (Algorithm1 line1,4) -- textbook budget-triggered maintenance. retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(candidate-pair proposal via all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity, S3.2 'Candidate Pair Selection')+RANKING(arg-max most-similar-pair selection loop). mide_lectura=SI: downstream QA F1/EM/accuracy on the COMPRESSED store is the paper's entire evaluation currency (Table1) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F. alcance=SESION (LoCoMo/LongMemEvalS multi-session, plus 3x/10x SCALED conversation-length stress tests). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the LLM judge's core function is EXPLICITLY to verify factual consistency/redundancy between memory entries ('decides, based on FACTUAL CONTENT rather than surface wording, whether it should be deleted, merged, or preserved', S1) -- squarely FIDELIDAD ('costuras'/consistency between memory sources, rule7). Table1: MemRefine holds F1 nearly flat under moderate compression on standard LoCoMo (0.40->0.39 A-MEM-graph at 70% budget) while realized storage meets every target budget across both frameworks and 3 benchmark settings -> BENCHMARK-E2E+MEDICION-COSTO(realized-vs-target storage ratio tracked as a result). Fig.4: RuleSim/RulePR rule-based ablation baselines (same candidate-pair loop, heuristic instead of LLM judgment) underperform MemRefine at every budget, isolating the LLM judge's necessity -> ABLATION; Fig.3 category-wise F1-change breakdown is a further controlled analysis. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text confirms both and adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD.

benchmarks: LongMemEval-S; own synthetic confound study (60 train / 60 test cases, 4 gold + 16 distractors each)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's central contribution IS exposing a measurement pitfall as the 'failure mode': 'scoring goal relevance against the held-out evaluation question -- an oracle that peeks at the future query -- saturates gold-evidence retention at ~0.98... this measures RETRIEVAL, not FORGETTING' (Abstract/S4.2); a real agent has not seen the evaluation question at consolidation time, so query-defined retention benchmarks cannot, on their own, demonstrate a forgetting advantage. Mitigated via the blind evaluation protocol, where goal relevance is computed only against consolidation-time-available information (session topic), revealing that similarity-only and recency-only policies 'collapse toward the chance floor' (0.286 and 0.368 respectively vs. 0.30 random) while the learned multi-factor value retains 0.770.
cita: Chen and Cheng (2026). Learning What to Remember: A Cognitively Grounded Multi-Factor Value Model for Agentic Memory.
notes: S3.1/Eq.1-2: each memory m (a stored conversational turn) is scored by a learned linear value V(m)=sum(wi*fi(m)) over 7 cognitively-grounded factors (emotional intensity, goal relevance, self/user relevance, reliability populated API-free; value alignment, task utility, usage history held at 0 in these experiments, table1) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA (memory items are individual conversational turns from LongMemEval-S's multi-session histories, flagged gold-evidence turns). representacion=VECTOR (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings drive the goal-relevance/self-relevance factors). operaciones=WRITE(S3.2 'Encoding depth: higher-value items are encoded more deeply' into 4 tiers at write time, the PROPOSED framework mechanism)+OLVIDO(Eq.3 explicit forget score = recency x usage x 1/value; 'items with the highest forget score are dropped first when the store exceeds budget' -- this IS the mechanism the paper's own experiment directly tests, S4.2) -- NO ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION/ACTUALIZACION tested or described (the paper explicitly isolates ONLY the budgeted keep/drop decision: 'we do not run an answerer or the full encode/forget/retrieve loop here', S4.2). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: a fixed keep-fraction budget kappa (e.g. 30%) explicitly gates which items are forgotten (Eq.3, S4.2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(sentence-transformer cosine similarity for goal/self-relevance factors)+RANKING(V(m) ranks candidates for both the keep/drop decision AND, per S3.2, retrieval rank). mide_lectura=NO: the paper explicitly frames MEASURING RETRIEVAL as the pitfall to avoid -- 'the oracle regime... measures retrieval, not forgetting' -- and its own blind-regime headline metric deliberately isolates the WRITE-time forgetting/retention decision without running any answerer or retrieval step ('we report gold-evidence retention rather than QA accuracy', explicit Limitation L1: 'retention is a proxy for end-task accuracy, not downstream QA correctness'); RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO therefore NOT required in F. alcance=SESION (LongMemEval-S multi-session chat histories, ~500 turns/case). multiagente=NO. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: the 'reliability' factor is explicitly a 'provenance heuristic (user-stated > model-stated)' (Table1) -- a direct provenance/source-trust mechanism -> FIDELIDAD in F. Table3: in the realistic BLIND regime, learned multi-factor value retains 0.770+-0.011 of gold evidence across 479 usable cases vs 0.657(uniform)/0.518(best single factor, self-relevance)/0.368(recency)/0.286(goal-only, near the 0.30 chance floor) -- every per-case bootstrap gap's 95% CI excludes zero -> BENCHMARK-E2E. Section4.1 synthetic confound study (planted value-alignment/self-relevance confounds) shows the gradient-free learner recovers 1.00 retention vs uniform-weighting's 0.62 and all single-factor baselines' 0.00 -> ABLATION; Section4.2's linear-vs-MLP nonlinear-value ablation shows a statistical TIE (+0.003, 55% of splits) -> further ABLATION. NEGATIVO in F: the near-chance-floor collapse of similarity/recency-only policies under realistic (blind) conditions is direct P5-style negative evidence that today's dominant single-factor production memory policies are fundamentally MIS-SPECIFIED for the forgetting decision. F_screening was CONSOLIDACION;COSTO; full text does NOT support either (no true multi-item merge/consolidation operation is tested, and no $/token cost is measured -- CPU-only/no-API-calls is a qualitative design property, not a measured cost outcome) so BOTH are DROPPED, and WRITE, FIDELIDAD, NEGATIVO are added.
